items.title: Artemis II crew to hold press conference from deep space tonight

featured_image.name: WATCH: NASA holds daily Artemis II news conference after releasing ...

items.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are coasting back toward Earth on Wednesday after completing a record-breaking lunar flyby, with the crew scheduled to hold their first in-space press conference later tonight as they near the end of a 10-day voyage around the moon.

The 20-minute virtual news conference is set for 9:45 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 8, with NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, answering media questions from roughly 200,000 miles away.[1]

items.title: UAE demands Iran pay reparations after 40 days of attacks

featured_image.name: UAE has an active role in Iran war and will be pounded if US ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates on Wednesday demanded that Iran be held "accountable and fully liable for damages and reparations" following weeks of devastating aerial attacks, as Abu Dhabi sought clarity on the terms of a fragile two-week ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump.

In an official statement, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the "unprovoked Iranian attacks targeting infrastructure, energy facilities, and civilian sites over the past 40 days — which included 2,819 ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones — and the resulting loss of life and property damage, necessitate a firm position". The ministry said it was seeking clarification from Washington on the ceasefire's provisions to ensure "Iran's full commitment to an immediate cessation of all hostilities in the region and the complete and unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz".[1]

items.title: Iran recloses Strait of Hormuz, threatening U.S. ceasefire

featured_image.name: Iran's parliament backs blocking Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Iran shut down the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, less than 24 hours after agreeing to a two-week ceasefire with the United States, casting immediate doubt over whether the fragile truce that ended more than five weeks of war could survive. Tehran cited Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon as a violation of the agreement, while Washington called the closure "completely unacceptable."[1][2]

The ceasefire, brokered with Pakistan's help and announced Tuesday evening just hours before a deadline set by President Donald Trump, had hinged on what the U.S. described as the "complete, immediate, and safe opening" of the strait — a waterway responsible for roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply. Iran confirmed it would allow passage "in coordination with Iranian armed forces," but Israeli strikes on Beirut that killed more than 100 people overnight appeared to upend that commitment.[3][4][5]

items.title: Israel kills 254 in largest Lebanon strikes as ceasefire dispute erupts

featured_image.name: Aftermath of Israel's heaviest attacks in Lebanon conflict

items.description: Israel unleashed its most devastating wave of airstrikes on Lebanon on Wednesday, killing at least 254 people and wounding more than 1,160 others in what the Israeli military called its "largest coordinated wave of strikes" since the war began on March 2, according to Lebanon's Civil Defence. The assault, which struck over 100 targets across the country within 10 minutes, came just hours after a U.S.-Iran ceasefire took effect — and amid sharp disagreement over whether Lebanon was included in the deal.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: UK vows to restore shipping confidence in Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran ceasefire

featured_image.name: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer arrives in Saudi Arabia ...

items.description:
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper announced on Wednesday that the United Kingdom will work with the shipping, insurance, and energy sectors to restore confidence in the Strait of Hormuz "as quickly as possible" following a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran.[1][2]

"Iran must cease all mining, drone attacks, and other attempts to block commercial shipping in the Strait immediately," Cooper said in her statement.[3][4]

items.title: NATO chief Rutte meets Trump amid US threat to leave alliance

featured_image.name: Trump is expected to meet with Rutte as he muses about pulling out ...

items.description:
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte arrived at the White House on Wednesday for what may be the most consequential meeting in the alliance's 77-year history, as President Donald Trump's threats to withdraw the United States from the military bloc have plunged transatlantic relations into uncharted territory.

The meeting, confirmed by NATO and the Associated Press, comes after Trump told Reuters and The Telegraph in recent interviews that he is "absolutely" considering pulling the US out of NATO, citing what he called "disgust" with the alliance over European members' refusal to support the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran, launched on February 28. "I was never swayed by NATO," Trump said. "I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way."[1][2]

items.title: Vance to lead US delegation in Iran talks in Islamabad

featured_image.name: US Vice President Vance spoke to intermediaries about Iran ...

items.description: The United States and Iran are preparing for their first face-to-face negotiations since the outbreak of war, with Vice President JD Vance set to lead the American delegation to Islamabad this weekend for talks aimed at forging a lasting peace agreement. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf will head Tehran's team, according to Iran's semi-official ISNA news agency. The high-stakes diplomacy follows a two-week ceasefire agreed to on Tuesday night, brokered largely through Pakistan's mediation.[1][2]

items.title: UN envoy arrives in Iran amid fragile US ceasefire

featured_image.name: UN chief names Arnault as ME envoy

items.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres's personal envoy Jean Arnault has arrived in Iran as part of a regional tour aimed at supporting "a comprehensive and durable resolution" to the conflict engulfing the Middle East, the United Nations announced on Wednesday. The visit comes amid a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran brokered just one day earlier with Pakistan's mediation.[1][2][3][4]

The accusation came as Israel launched what its military called its largest wave of strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon since the war began, hitting 100 targets in 10 minutes.[1][2][3]
